I will keep to the wheat-maize rotation on my land this year. In Quzhou County, this is the cropping pattern I know best, and at my age I value something steady, familiar, and easy to manage with local machinery and local buyers. I will finish managing my winter wheat through spring with moderate water and fertilizer, then harvest it in early summer and plant summer maize right away on the same land. I will use improved seed instead of anything fancy, because I want reliable emergence and stable yield, not extra risk or extra management. I will not spread myself across too many crops, because I do not want more labor, more market uncertainty, or more technical trouble than necessary.

For wheat, I will keep inputs moderate. I will give nitrogen in split applications, enough phosphorus for roots, and some potassium so the crop stands better and fills grain better. I will irrigate only a few times because water matters and I do not want to waste money. I will spray only when needed for common diseases and pests. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize, because timing matters a lot for yield here. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, give enough nitrogen for strong growth, and keep phosphorus and potassium at moderate levels. I will irrigate a bit more if the summer turns dry, and I will control weeds and insects with a few targeted sprays. I will stay with rotary tillage because it is what I can manage efficiently and it fits this double-cropping system.
